hook.from: Geography > Location, Terrain, Natural resources; Economy > Exports
hook.excerpt: Western Africa, bordering the North Atlantic Ocean, between Senegal and Western Sahara || mostly barren, flat plains of the Sahara; some central hills || Mauritania is considered part of both North Africa's Maghreb region and West Africa's Sahel region; most of the population is concentrated in the cities of Nouakchott and Nouadhibou and along the Senegal River in the southern part of the country || Resources: iron ore, gypsum, copper, phosphate, diamonds, gold, oil, fish || Exports: gold, iron ore, fish, processed crustaceans, copper ore (2023)

physicalGeography.excerpt: mostly barren, flat plains of the Sahara; some central hills || Western Africa, bordering the North Atlantic Ocean, between Senegal and Western Sahara

climate.excerpt: desert; constantly hot, dry, dusty || hot, dry, dust/sand-laden sirocco wind primarily in March and April; periodic droughts

economy.excerpt: lower middle-income West African economy; primarily agrarian; rising urbanization; poor property rights; systemic corruption; endemic social and workforce tensions; wide-scale terrorism; foreign over-fishing; environmentally fragile || Exports: gold, iron ore, fish, processed crustaceans, copper ore (2023) || Industries: fish processing, oil production, mining (iron ore, gold, copper)

peopleAndCulture.from: People and Society > Languages, Religions, Ethnic groups, Urbanization
peopleAndCulture.excerpt: Muslim (official) 100% || Black Moors (Haratines - Arabic-speaking descendants of African origin who are or were enslaved by White Moors) 40%, White Moors (of Arab-Amazigh descent, known as Beydane) 30%, Sub-Saharan Mauritanians (non-Arabic speaking, largely resident in or originating from the Senegal River Valley, including Halpulaar, Fulani, Soninke, Wolof, and Bambara ethnic groups) 30%
